label: Sunday, November 1, 2026 · Elections-eve edition
intro: Good morning. It's Sunday, November 1st. Here's your Read Daily brief.

items.title: A big sell-off collides with more Big Tech earnings and a midterm election: What to watch this week
items.take: A bruising week for tech rolls into a heavy calendar: Apple reports Monday with its new CEO at the helm, the midterm elections land Tuesday, and the October jobs report closes the week Friday. All eyes are on what could re-light the fire under the tech sector, and the fire here is the bad kind.

items.title: Wall Street Week Ahead: Midterm Madness, Nvidia, and Walmart
items.take: Midterms and the October jobs report dominate, with payrolls expected to rise 65K and unemployment holding at 4.2%. Earnings from Apple, AMD and Palantir test the battered tech trade, and the weekend question is blunt: can Anthropic’s IPO save the market?

items.title: The Week That Was, The Week Ahead: Anthropic’s S-1 in focus
items.take: Investors are still digesting Anthropic’s IPO paperwork: more than $16 billion of revenue in the first half of 2026, against a reported net loss of $80.7 billion, largely from a one-time accounting adjustment. It is the clearest public look yet at what the AI boom earns and burns.

items.title: How suspected North Korean hackers swiped billions
items.take: The Post retraces how the record Binance theft, now estimated at $6.3 billion, moved in minutes across blockchains with automated laundering. Crypto stocks were down more than 6% Friday and the story follows the money into the weekend.

items.title: Gulf nations push to stave off re-escalation of Iran war
items.take: With reports of a possible strike window after the midterms, Gulf states are working to keep the Iran conflict from hitting their doorstep again. For markets it is the biggest non-AI wildcard: a re-escalation would tighten oil further and keep inflation an issue.

items.title: Making Sense: Sponsors, spreads and stress testing: Navigating 2026’s rate reset
items.take: Today’s rotation pick asks the question behind Friday’s rout: in volatile markets, do you pay for certainty now or preserve flexibility for later. Leveraged finance and private markets are weighing exactly that trade-off in a higher-for-longer rate world.
